name: Grinner Blocks
author: Haider Shah

sections.description:
See every block and effect in action at grinner.io.

Why Grinner Blocks

  • Performance-first: many blocks ship no JavaScript at all, and each block’s CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that use it.
  • Everything is included — no paid tier, no locked features.
  • Native blocks in the editor you already use. Deactivate the plugin and your posts keep their content; the controls added to core blocks simply switch off.
  • Landing-page features: content sliders, hover lists, card piles, progress bars, animated marquees, before/after sliders, counters, scroll reveals, avatar stacks and more.
  • You edit everything directly: place a block, drag it, change its text.

Everything you need to build landing pages

Grinner Blocks is a set of native blocks and controls for building and launching modern landing pages in WordPress. It lives inside the block editor you already use — no page builder, no jQuery. Every block renders on the server where it can, and each block’s own CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that use it. On block themes, the shared styles also load only where a page uses them, leaving about half a kilobyte site-wide; classic themes still load 82 KB of shared styles on every page.

Blocks

  • Before / After — two-image comparison slider, side by side or top and bottom, with a draggable divider driven by a real range input so it works with a keyboard and a screen reader. On touch screens the page still scrolls freely across it. Zero layout shift.
  • Avatar Stack — overlapping avatars for social proof, in a straight row or a gentle arc, with an optional “+N” chip, a trailing label and hover effects. It shrinks to fit narrow screens. No front-end JavaScript.
  • Logo Marquee — a continuous scrolling row of logos, pausing on hover, on keyboard focus and when scrolled off-screen.
  • Image Slider — the same continuous loop for photography, with fades, captions, hover effects and optional links. It can run along a curve (Arc, Smile, Drum or Wave), or stand still and let visitors swipe through it, looping endlessly.
  • Text Rotator — a line of text that cycles through a list, one item at a time, with fades, blurs, clip reveals or the Pixel Reveal and Decrypt effects — on a clock, or as the page scrolls. It can play an entrance animation first, its lines can carry formatting and accents, and it follows the alignment of the layout it sits in. Visitors who prefer reduced motion see the first item, still.
  • Image Rotator — a stepped carousel showing up to six images at a time, advancing on its own, with arrows, or both. Eight transitions (Carousel Flow can rest in an arc), plus layouts that arrange the images as a deck, a polaroid scatter, a mosaic, stepped columns, a spotlight with thumbnails or an orbit. Pause on hover, and no autoplay for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
  • Scrolling Text — a marquee for words, with separators, tilt and per-item styling.
  • Countdown — counts down to a date in any timezone, ticking live in the browser while a permanent screen-reader line states the real deadline.
  • Video Embed — a click-to-load YouTube facade using youtube-nocookie.com. Nothing from YouTube runs until the visitor clicks; a poster and play badge stand in until then.
  • Lottie — a self-hosted Lottie player supporting .json and .dotlottie, with loop / once / hover playback, a poster fallback and a mobile kill switch. The player library loads only when an animation starts, and you choose whether it starts once the page has loaded or on the visitor’s first touch or scroll.
  • Icon — one inline SVG icon from a bundled set of 1,512, rendered server-side in six weights.
  • Table — a responsive table built from real blocks, so each cell can hold anything, with an outer border and column widths.
  • Hover List — big link rows that show each row’s image on hover or keyboard focus. Five presets: a work index whose image follows the cursor, a split layout with one image area, a background swap, inline thumbnails, and expanding panels — an accordion that opens on hover, by click, tap or keyboard.
  • Content Slider — slides that hold any blocks (testimonials, features, case studies), moved by swipe, arrows, dots or autoplay. Four layouts: full width, several with a peek, a centred slide, or cards with a progress bar. It rewinds at the end instead of cloning slides, and its script loads only when arrows, dots or autoplay are on.
  • Card Pile — cards that stick and pile up as the page scrolls, for process steps or chapters. Four presets, CSS only, no JavaScript.
  • Progress Bar — labelled bars, thick bars, segments and steps, or rings, drawn in as the page scrolls or once in view. Values as a percentage, “42 of 60”, money or a rating, printed as real text.

Responsive layout controls

  • Set a maximum width per device — desktop, tablet and mobile — on headings, paragraphs, groups and columns.
  • Align a width-limited block left, centre or right with a box-alignment control.
  • Set how many columns a Grid block shows on desktop, tablet and mobile, with an optional gap for each.
  • Reorder the children of a Columns or Grid block on mobile without touching the desktop layout — per item, or with a one-switch reverse.
  • Choose when Columns stack: on phones only, on tablets as well, or two columns on tablets.

Block enhancements

Added as extra controls on the core blocks you already use:

  • Entrance animations and reveal-on-scroll for headings, paragraphs and groups, including the word-by-word Assemble effect, plus a number counter that counts up or shuffles its digits.
  • Accent text: select words and give them an accent from the toolbar — six ready-made styles built from your theme’s fonts and colours, or accents saved on your site — with highlights, underlines, circles, gradient or outline text and a draw-in animation. Each decoration has its own size and position controls, and changing an accent changes only the words you selected.
  • Grey to Colour: words go from muted to full colour as a heading or paragraph scrolls up the screen. No JavaScript, and the text is always readable.
  • Script text effects for headings and paragraphs — Pixel Reveal, Line Reveal, Decrypt and Typewriter — that hold the text’s exact layout while they run.
  • Button hover effects with their own fill and text colours, icons with their own colours, decorative corner marks, full-width fixes, vertical stacking, and click-to-play video buttons. On phones, a tapped button shows its hover colours while pressed and then returns to normal.
  • Navigation hover styles and markers, and item pills such as “New” or “Hot” beside a menu link; a sticky header with an optional glass effect.
  • A sticky call-to-action bar, whose buttons can stretch across the bar on phones, and clickable Group / Columns blocks: in a Query Loop each card can link to its own post, and a clickable card is one link and one Tab stop, while buttons to other pages still work on their own.
  • Layout reveals, text gradients and inline text icons.
  • Animated backgrounds for Group and Cover blocks: slow gradients, blobs and grain in your palette’s colours, paused off screen and still for reduced motion.
  • Link hover cards: internal links in paragraphs and lists can show a small preview card on hover or keyboard focus.
  • An aspect ratio and a rotation for the Group block, opacity for palette text colours, a paragraph pinned over its section, and Keep still for one child of a Parallax group.
  • Image effects on the core Image block: hover tilt, zoom, lift, greyscale and glare; parallax; entrances such as Rise, Wipe and Roll; and scroll effects such as zoom, tilt in and grey to colour. Images can also take a maximum width with limits, a resting angle, and stickers pinned over a section, still or animated.
  • A Loading setting on the Image, Cover and Post Featured Image blocks — Auto, Lazy, Eager or Priority — so you decide which image loads first. In a Query Loop, Priority applies to the first card only.

Site settings

  • Header and footer code injection, gated on the unfiltered_html capability.
  • Smooth anchor scrolling with a scroll offset for sticky headers.
  • Simple exact-match redirects.
  • A site-wide switch for animated previews inside the editor.
  • Preload the heading font (Performance): one preload for the font your main heading uses. Off by default.
  • An optional Excerpt field for pages, so Query Loop cards can show a summary you write.
  • A Data setting to keep or wipe your plugin data when you uninstall — off by default, so your data is kept.

Performance and accessibility

Every block’s CSS and JavaScript loads only on pages that actually use it, and the stylesheets and scripts visitors download carry no developer comments. The blocks use only font weights your site already loads, so they never add a font file. Many blocks ship no JavaScript at all, and one shared IntersectionObserver drives every scroll effect. Exactly one image per page is ever marked as the priority image, so nothing competes for the browser’s attention. Content is never hidden waiting for a script, even when a caching plugin delays JavaScript, and nothing Grinner Blocks animates can make a page scroll sideways on a phone. Animated content is hidden from screen readers and paired with a static equivalent, anything that moves on its own can be paused from the keyboard, and every animation stops for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

External services

Grinner Blocks connects to one external service, YouTube (operated by Google), and only on pages where you have added a YouTube video: a Grinner Video Embed block, or a click-to-play video on a button, an image or a Lottie animation. No other external service is contacted, and nothing is sent anywhere by the plugin’s own server code.

  • Video thumbnails. When a Grinner Video Embed block has no custom poster image, its poster is YouTube’s thumbnail for that video, loaded from i.ytimg.com when a visitor views the page, and in the editor while you edit the block. The request comes from the visitor’s browser, so YouTube receives the video ID, the visitor’s IP address and standard browser information. Choose a poster from your Media Library and no thumbnail request is made.
  • Video playback. The player loads from youtube-nocookie.com only after a visitor clicks play; before that click nothing from YouTube runs. On that click YouTube receives the video ID, the visitor’s IP address and standard browser information, and the player is then governed by YouTube’s own terms. If JavaScript is unavailable, the play button is a plain link to the video on youtube.com.

YouTube Terms of Service: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Source

All first-party Grinner Blocks code ships in this plugin as it was written: plain, human-readable PHP, JavaScript and CSS, with no compilation. This covers everything under blocks/, enhancements/, admin/, inc/blocks-layer2.php, inc/settings.php, inc/redirects.php, grinner-blocks.php and uninstall.php.

Since 1.7.0, visitors are served comment-free copies of the front-end stylesheets and scripts. Each copy (*.min.css, *.min.js) sits next to its readable source file in the same folder, and is made from it by removing only comments and extra whitespace: names, strings and code are unchanged. The copies are made by the plugin’s own build scripts, bin/build-css.js and bin/build-js.js (Node.js; the script build reads the code with the acorn parser to find what is a comment), which are development tools and are not included in the plugin. The readable file beside each copy is the source.

Three sets of files are pre-built third-party code. Their readable source lives upstream:

  • lottie-web 5.12.2 — blocks/lottie/assets/lottie.min.js is the official lottie_light.min.js build from release 5.12.2, unmodified (the “light” build omits the expression evaluator). Source: https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-web — released under the MIT license.
  • fflate 0.8.2 — blocks/lottie/assets/fflate.min.js is the official umd/index.js build from release 0.8.2, unmodified. Used to unpack .lottie archives in the browser. Source: https://github.com/101arrowz/fflate — released under the MIT license.
  • Twentig 2.0.1 — everything under dist/ is the built asset output of the Twentig plugin, version 2.0.1, which Grinner Blocks forks. Source: https://wordpress.org/plugins/twentig/ — released under GPL-3.0-or-later. Three files carry first-party modifications: in dist/index.css the editor icon embedded in it was changed from Twentig’s mark to the plugin’s own mark; in dist/style-index.css and dist/blocks/common.css the block entrance animation’s hidden starting state applies only once the plugin’s script has marked the page, so content is never left hidden when scripts are delayed or off. Upstream files the plugin does not use (starter-site templates and their preview images) are left out; every other file under dist/ is unchanged from the upstream 2.0.1 release.

The icon artwork data under enhancements/_shared/phosphor/ is generated from Phosphor Icons 2.1.1 (https://github.com/phosphor-icons/core, MIT) and ships as plain, readable JSON — see manifest.json there for the exact source version and generation date.

Credits

Grinner Blocks includes code from Twentig by Twentig.com, used under the GPL.

Bundled third-party libraries and their licenses are listed under Source, above.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the grinner-blocks folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate through the Plugins menu
  3. Go to Grinner Blocks in your WordPress admin menu, then add any Grinner block in the editor
sections.faq:
Is Grinner Blocks really free? Is anything locked behind a paid tier?

Every block, control and setting is free and included. There is no pro version, no locked features, and no account to create. The plugin is complete on its own.

What happens to my content if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Your posts and pages keep everything you wrote, and the controls Grinner Blocks adds to core blocks simply switch off — your core content is untouched. The plugin’s own blocks, like Before / After, need the plugin active to display: while it’s deactivated they show a placeholder, and they come straight back the moment you reactivate, with nothing lost. Deleting the plugin keeps your redirects and your header/footer code, so reinstalling restores them — unless you first turn on “Delete all plugin data” under Grinner Blocks → Data.

Do I need a page builder?

No. Grinner Blocks works entirely inside the standard WordPress block editor. There’s nothing new to learn — the blocks and controls appear alongside the core ones.

Does it work with the block editor I already have?

Yes. It uses the standard WordPress block editor (Gutenberg) — no separate editor, no special mode, no shortcodes.

Will it work with my theme?

It’s tested with WordPress’s native block themes and should be compatible with any block-based theme. Grinner Blocks adds blocks and controls; it doesn’t replace your theme or take over your layout.

Will it slow my site down?

It’s built to avoid that. Many blocks ship no JavaScript at all, and each block’s CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that use it.

Does it work with caching and optimisation plugins?

Yes, with one setting to check. Grinner Blocks uses native image-loading attributes, so it works alongside caching and optimisation plugins. When an optimiser delays JavaScript, your content still shows straight away and the animations play once the scripts run. After you update Grinner Blocks, it clears LiteSpeed Cache’s page and CSS/JS caches once, so visitors get the new styles. If you run a LiteSpeed-class optimiser with image lazy-loading turned on, add “ilm-eager” to its lazy-load class-name exclusions — Grinner Blocks marks every image meant to load immediately (a hero poster or an above-the-fold marquee) with that class, and the exclusion lets those images load straight away instead of being deferred. If your optimiser also picks priority (“LCP”) images on its own, the two can overlap. On LiteSpeed, that feature can stay active for logged-out visitors even with its own setting switched off, so check your page’s source rather than the settings screen. Grinner Blocks never changes your optimiser’s settings for you.

How do I keep a font size from shrinking on phones?

WordPress makes most font sizes fluid, so they shrink on small screens. For a size that never shrinks on phones, add a Font size preset in Styles with Fluid typography off, and pick it in Grinner’s font size controls like any other size.

Is there an accordion that opens on hover?

Yes: the Hover List block’s Expanding panels preset. Panels open when the mouse rests on them, and also by click, tap and keyboard. WordPress’s own Accordion block opens on click.

Where do I get help?

Ask on the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org — post your question there and we’ll answer it directly.
sections.changelog:
1.8.0

  • New: Hover List block. Big link rows that show each row’s image on hover or keyboard focus, in five presets: Work index (the image follows the cursor), Split, Background swap, Inline thumbnail, and Expanding panels — an accordion that opens on hover, by click, tap or keyboard.
  • New: Content Slider block. Slides that hold any blocks, moved by swipe, arrows, dots or autoplay, in four layouts: Full width, Peek, Centred and Cards. It rewinds at the end instead of cloning slides. Autoplay is on by default for Full width only, and can always be paused.
  • New: Card Pile block. Cards that stick and pile up as the page scrolls, in four presets: Straight, Recede, Dealt and Split. CSS only, with a Loading setting for the first card’s image, Lazy by default.
  • New: Progress Bar block. Labelled bars, thick bars, segments and steps, or rings, drawn in as the page scrolls, once in view, or not at all. Values as a percentage, “42 of 60”, money ($ by default) or a rating.
  • New: Image Rotator layouts: Deck, Polaroid scatter, Mosaic (window or 2×2), Stepped columns, Spotlight and Orbit, with Gap between cards, and Tilt, Depth and Ring spread for Orbit. Image Height now sizes every layout.
  • New: A curved track for the Image Slider: Arc, Smile, Drum or Wave, with a depth, and images that stay upright or lean with the curve. CSS only.
  • New: Scroll mode for the Text Rotator: the line changes as the page scrolls from the top, or as the line crosses the screen, instead of on a clock. CSS only.
  • New: Animated backgrounds for Group and Cover blocks: slow gradients, blobs and grain in your palette’s colours, with a speed and a strength. They pause off screen and stand still for reduced motion.
  • New: Link hover cards. Internal links in paragraphs and lists can show a small preview card on hover or keyboard focus, in three designs. Phones keep the plain link.
  • New: An aspect ratio and a rotation for the Group block, a paragraph pinned over its section, Keep still for one child of a Parallax group, opacity for palette text colours, and a fixed size for accent text.
  • New: Scrolling Text gets a box of its own (background, padding, border and radius from Styles), the Table an outer border and column widths, and the Countdown a label case, a label position and a size on phones.
  • New: “This post or page” links for the Clickable Block and the Icon block. In a Query Loop each card links to its own post.
  • New: Preload the heading font, under Grinner Blocks → Performance (off by default): one preload for the font file your main heading uses.
  • Improved: A clickable card is one link and one Tab stop. Links inside it to the same page become part of the card, screen readers hear the post title, and keyboard focus shows a ring around the whole card. Buttons that go somewhere else still work on their own.
  • Improved: Anything that moves on its own can be paused from the keyboard. An autoplaying Image Slider or Logo Marquee takes keyboard focus, and focus pauses it.
  • Improved: The Hover List’s hover colour also works with Dim the others and Shift the title.
  • Improved: The editor tells you when an image set to load first sits in slide 2 or later of a Content Slider, where it always loads lazily.
  • Improved: Lighter default images in the Image Slider and Image Rotator: 137.7 KB down to 19.6 KB.
  • Improved: The new blocks use only font weights your site already loads, so they never add a font file.
  • Improved: docs/settings-map.json covers every new setting, with help text, ranges and conditions that match the editor.
  • Changed: A Text Rotator that changes with scrolling plays no entrance animation, because the two clashed. The saved entrance comes back if you switch it to Over time.
  • Changed: Countdown labels are never smaller than 11px, so a small timer stays readable.
  • Changed: The Image Rotator’s Pixel Reveal cover colour is retired: the dissolve is made from the images themselves, so the colour no longer had any effect.
  • Fixed: Reduced motion now stops the Text Rotator, Image Slider, Logo Marquee and Scrolling Text; they used to keep moving.
  • Fixed: Re-saving a post no longer drops older Twentig settings saved with it.
  • Fixed: A Table with only a corner radius keeps its outer line.

1.7.0

  • New: Accent text. Select words and apply an accent from the toolbar: six ready-made styles (serif italic, marker, underline, squiggle, circle and gradient) that use your theme’s fonts and colours, or accents saved on your site, with highlights, lines and circles, gradient or outline text, a size and a draw-in animation. Each highlight, line, circle and border has size and position controls, with a live preview. Changes in the Accent panel apply to the selected words only; anyone who can edit a page can save a look as a new accent, and administrators change or delete accents site-wide in the Site accents screen. Accented words can be kept on one line, and accents work with every text effect.
  • New: Grey to Colour text effect. Words go from muted to full colour, word by word in reading order, as a heading or paragraph of up to 150 words scrolls up the screen. No JavaScript, and the text is always readable.
  • New: More hover options on the core Image block. Tilt has eight directions, a strength and a depth, and can follow the mouse; Zoom has an amount and a starting point, and can follow the cursor; a glare sheen and a hover speed are new. Linked images show their hover effect on keyboard focus too.
  • New: Image entrances: Fade, Rise, Settle, Wipe, Soft blur, Slide and Roll. An image the page shows straight away uses a movement-only version, so it is never hidden while the page loads.
  • New: Image scroll effects: Zoom on scroll, Tilt in, Grey to colour, Expand to full, Wipe in and Roll. CSS only; they follow the image as it travels up the screen.
  • New: Image parallax, previously on or off, has a direction (down, up, left or right), a speed and a crop choice. “Break out of frame” moves the whole image past its neighbours instead of inside its frame.
  • New: Rotation for images: a resting angle, with its own angle on phones if you like. It is not an animation, so it stays when motion is reduced.
  • New: Never smaller than / Never larger than for an image’s Max width, so a size in % or vw stops where you want it.
  • New: Pinned stickers can hang over a rounded section’s edge, sit up to 400px out, or be inset by a percentage of the section or of the sticker itself; in Custom placement they can be positioned by their top-left corner.
  • New: A Loading setting on the Cover and Post Featured Image blocks, as on the Image block: Auto, Lazy, Eager or Priority. In a Query Loop, Priority and Eager apply to the first card and the other cards load as they scroll into view.
  • New: Entrance animations on the Text Rotator, the same set as headings. The rotation starts once the entrance has played, rotating lines can hold formatting and accents, and the block has a Text alignment control and follows the alignment of the Stack or Row it sits in.
  • New: Vertical Before / After. The divider moves up and down, with keyboard and touch support; the page still scrolls when you swipe across it.
  • New: Navigation item pills: “New”, “Hot”, “Beta” or your own text beside a menu link, inline or pinned to a corner, with full styling and an optional pulse. Screen readers hear the label naturally.
  • New: Arc layout for the Avatar Stack, with a Curve control, and an Arc resting tilt for the Image Rotator’s Carousel Flow transition.
  • New: A Start setting for Lottie: start automatically once the page has loaded, or on the visitor’s first touch or scroll.
  • New: A Text colour for button hover animations, next to the Fill colour, so a light fill never leaves white text unreadable. Hover Colour also works on a button with no hover animation, for a simple colour change.
  • New: An Icon colour and a Hover icon colour for button icons. Left unset, the icon follows the button’s text colour, as before.
  • New: “Stretch buttons on mobile” for the Sticky CTA: on phones the bar’s buttons share its full width, or each run full width when stacked. Off by default.
  • New: A “Stack at” choice for Columns in Grinner Responsive: stack on tablets as well as phones, or show two columns on tablets.
  • New: Scrolling Text uses WordPress’s own Size and Font controls (Styles tab, Typography), so it gets every size and font from Styles, fluid sizes included. Sizes chosen before keep their meaning.
  • New: Palette colours stay linked. A colour picked from your palette in any Grinner setting is saved as that palette colour, so it changes when you change the palette in Styles. Custom colours, and colours saved before, work as they did.
  • New: Before / After takes a corner radius; Countdown takes a font, weight, letter spacing and letter case from Typography; Table cells take their own colours and vertical alignment; a Table’s padding can differ on tablets and phones, and its staggered entrance has a step and can go row by row. Lift hover has a Shadow switch, and the Accordion has a Focus ring setting.
  • New: Page excerpts. A switch under Grinner Blocks → Editor adds WordPress’s own Excerpt field to pages, so Query Loop cards and the Post Excerpt block can show a summary you write. Off by default; turning it off keeps any excerpts you wrote. SEO plugins may use a written excerpt as the page’s description.
  • New: docs/settings-map.json lists every Grinner setting, its panel, its label and exactly what it stores, for developers and AI tools that build pages. Nothing loads it on your site.
  • Improved: Visitors get comment-free copies of Grinner’s stylesheets and scripts. The front-end stylesheets go from about 473 KB to 195 KB and the front-end scripts from about 180 KB to 74 KB. The readable source files are still in the plugin.
  • Improved: The Lottie player library loads only when an animation starts, and an animation on the first screen waits until the page has loaded, so pages with Lottie appear much sooner.
  • Improved: Preload, preconnect and dns-prefetch links in your Header code are placed at the very top of the page, before any styles, so preloaded files start downloading sooner. The rest of your Header code stays where it was.
  • Improved: Images placed by Grinner Blocks count towards WordPress’s “load the first few images straight away” rule, so images further down a page load lazily, and only one image per page is ever given priority, even when the same picture appears in several blocks.
  • Improved: The Image Rotator downloads the next image at the size it will show, not the full original.
  • Improved: After Grinner Blocks is updated, LiteSpeed Cache’s page and CSS/JS caches are cleared once, so visitors get the new styles. Nothing happens on sites without LiteSpeed Cache, and its settings are never changed.
  • Improved: Content is never hidden from first-time visitors when a caching plugin delays JavaScript: headings, sections and images show at once and animate once the scripts run.
  • Improved: On phones, Hero Mode keeps first-screen text still for the Pixel Reveal, Line Reveal, Decrypt and Typewriter effects. A Text Rotator’s Pixel Reveal or Decrypt transition changes lines plainly until the visitor’s first scroll or tap, then plays.
  • Improved: On phones and tablets, a button shows its hover colours while it is pressed and then returns to its own colours, instead of turning black and staying black after a tap.
  • Improved: Slide Fill and Circle Expand with no Fill colour use your theme’s button hover colour from Styles, and button colours set in Styles with transparency or color-mix() are followed.
  • Changed: Slide Fill and Circle Expand with a light Fill colour and no Text colour show dark text on hover (your theme’s contrast colour) instead of white, when that reads better.
  • Changed: A Sticky column’s “Disable on mobile” is now “Pin on”: desktop only, desktop and tablet, or all screen sizes. Columns saved before keep what they did.
  • Changed: A Row that stacks on smaller screens lines its children up along its horizontal alignment, as WordPress does; vertical Stretch keeps them full width. Its gaps accept spacing presets and clamp().
  • Fixed: Grinner effects and blocks no longer make a page scroll sideways on phones, including pinned stickers, corner marks, rotating text, sideways animations, full-width bands and Image Sliders with side padding.
  • Fixed: The Logo Marquee, Image Slider and Scrolling Text no longer stretch a card or column they sit in to thousands of pixels wide.
  • Fixed: An Image Slider set to manual scroll loops endlessly on block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five (it used to stop at the end), and crosses its loop point without a jump.
  • Fixed: An image sized with Max width keeps its size in a Row beside long text, up to half the Row and never beyond the photo’s own size; it used to shrink.
  • Fixed: An SVG in an Image block that WordPress has no size for is no longer invisible as a pinned sticker, centred or in a row: it takes the size set in its file, and elsewhere fills its column as before. An SVG’s Max width is now its size; for photos it stays a cap.
  • Fixed: A group in Hero Mode with Stagger children plays its children’s entrance on desktop; they used to stay still.
  • Fixed: Hover on each card no longer cancels a staggered entrance on the same group.
  • Fixed: Buttons using Slide Fill, Text Flip, Grow or Circle Expand show your site’s button colour from Styles.
  • Fixed: Hover effects on buttons styled in Styles: Grow keeps the button’s own shape and hover colours; Text Flip shows the label in your button’s text colour and no longer crops it with a tight line height; Ghost Fill fills with your button’s own colours and shows its outline on phones and in the editor too; a gradient button’s fill slides in over the gradient.
  • Fixed: Text Flip on a button with formatted text flips the label as one unit, formatting included, and pressing a Text Flip button with a mouse no longer drops it back to its resting colour.
  • Fixed: Buttons with Slide Fill, Text Flip or Circle Expand are no taller than the button, so their bottom corner marks sit on its corners and a row of mixed buttons lines up.
  • Fixed: Only the image you mark Priority gets high priority. A featured image shown above the content no longer takes a second high-priority slot, and on sites using LiteSpeed Cache the priority image keeps its head preload when the same picture also appears earlier on the page.
  • Fixed: The Video Embed, Lottie and Before / After blocks no longer disappear inside a Row or Stack, or inside a Group that sits in one; the Image Rotator and an Icon left at its default alignment follow the Row, Stack or Group they sit in; and a YouTube Shorts video is centred on your site as it is in the editor.
  • Fixed: A pinned sticker set to “Behind the content” sits behind the section’s text and in front of its background, on the page and in the editor; it used to paint over the text.
  • Fixed: Parallax on a group’s children keeps pinned stickers where they were placed, and parallax on an image narrower than its column no longer shows the zoomed picture past the image’s own edge.
  • Fixed: The Grinner Table is read as a table by screen readers (rows, column headers, row headers and cells), with an optional Table name. It looks the same.
  • Fixed: The Avatar Stack shrinks to fit a narrow screen instead of running off the side.
  • Fixed: Scrolling Text’s Full Width Breakout spans the whole screen even when the block has side margins or sits inside a constrained group.
  • Fixed: A Text Rotator set to a large size sits like a heading of the same size instead of leaving extra space above and below.
  • Fixed: Count up animates numbers written with their unit, such as 0.8s, 180KB or 3x.
  • Fixed: With the Accordion’s Open animation on, answers are spaced as without it.
  • Fixed: Line breaks inside headings and paragraphs using the Word by Word, Stagger Fade or Assemble effect are kept.
  • Fixed: On touch screens, scrolling the page across a Before / After slider no longer moves the divider.
  • Fixed: The Image Rotator no longer causes a layout shift each time its loop wraps, and images added without a web address (by a pattern or an import) show in the editor.
  • Fixed: Colour settings in the Before / After, Avatar Stack and Image Slider blocks accept colours only.
  • Fixed: Font size pickers in Grinner panels list the same sizes as WordPress’s own, including sizes added in Styles, and keep the size you pick when several share one base size.

1.6.1

  • New: Stickers on the core Image block: Spin, Rock, Float or Turn on scroll, pinned anywhere over a section by one of nine anchors and a nudge, in front of or behind the content, and optionally hidden on phones. A sticker never takes the page’s priority image slot.
  • New: Play button settings for the Video Embed: size, fill colour, ring colour and pulse spread.
  • Changed: Grinner Blocks now works with WordPress 6.5 and later.
  • Improved: Accordion answers slide shut as well as open.
  • Fixed: The Lottie block’s width now shows in the editor as it does on the page.
  • Fixed: Word by Word animates each word of formatted text separately instead of treating the formatted words as one.
  • Fixed: The Word by Word, Stagger Fade and Assemble effects show correctly on sites that remove unused CSS.
  • Fixed: A Lottie animation on the first screen no longer stays on its poster when scripts arrive late.
  • Under the hood: Output escaping tightened throughout, following the WordPress.org review.

1.6.0

  • Renamed: the plugin is now Grinner Blocks. Block titles, the inserter category, the settings panels and the admin menu use the new name, and the admin menu icon and settings heading show a G. Your blocks, settings, redirects and header/footer code carry over unchanged.
  • Changed: Grinner Blocks now requires PHP 8.0 or later.
  • New: Snap transition for the Image Rotator — each image changes in one step, with no movement in between.
  • Improved: The Image Rotator’s Pixel Reveal transition now plays in the editor preview.
  • New: The editor warns you when two blocks on a page both ask to load first — a Priority image, or a Lottie, Video Embed or Before / After block with “Above the fold” on. Only one image can load first, and it should be the largest one visible before scrolling.
  • Improved: An image you set to Priority now keeps the page’s priority slot even when an “Above the fold” block appears earlier on the page, and images too small to be the main image never take it.
  • Improved: An image block with no loading setting now leaves the choice to WordPress, which loads the first large images on a page immediately and the rest lazily. Previously such images were always lazy-loaded, including hero images at the top of the page. Images further down the page still load lazily.
  • Improved: A Priority image on a block theme starts downloading as soon as the page begins to load.
  • Improved: Images WordPress loads immediately now carry the “ilm-eager” marker, so optimisers that honour it don’t delay them.
  • Fixed: Line Reveal and Pixel Reveal now cover the text with your section’s background colour instead of white, so no pale line shows on coloured sections.
  • Fixed: Pixel Reveal and Line Reveal no longer paint outside the heading onto neighbouring content, or widen the page on phones.
  • Under the hood: Per-block styles for the Logo Marquee, Scrolling Text, Image Slider, Site Logo width and Accordion now come from stylesheets instead of style tags printed inside the page.

1.5.1

  • New: The Countdown block now counts down live in the editor, to exactly the moment your site counts down to. Turn it off for one block with “Preview animation in editor”, or for every block with the Animate previews switch under Grinner Blocks → Editor.
  • Improved: Faster hero images on block themes. When a Video Embed, Lottie or Before / After block has “Above the fold (hero)” turned on, its image starts downloading as soon as the page begins to load, instead of when the browser reaches it. Before / After fetches its “after” image, the one browsers measure as the page’s main image. Works alongside LiteSpeed Cache, including its WebP images, without downloading anything twice.
  • Improved: Lighter pages on block themes. The shared stylesheets inherited from Twentig, about 13.5 KB, now load only on pages that use them; every other page loads about half a kilobyte.
  • Improved: A more accurate plugin listing. A new External services section explains when YouTube is contacted, what it receives and how to avoid the thumbnail request. The loading and optimiser claims now match what the plugin actually does, and the website links to a site that no longer resolves are gone.
  • Fixed: Grinner Blocks and the Twentig plugin can now be active on the same site; previously, activating both caused a fatal error. Saved settings carry over automatically when you update.
  • Fixed: Sections using Stagger children with the Drop or Swing entrance no longer stay blank on pages that also use a text animation.
  • Fixed: Parallax inside a Group with rounded corners and an image now moves as you scroll instead of freezing.
  • Fixed: The Gradient sweep and Image zoom hover effects now show on Group and Columns blocks (including Row, Stack and Grid) that have a background colour or image. Applied to Children, Image zoom scales each card’s own background.
  • Fixed: The Countdown’s Left and Right alignment now takes effect inside a vertical Stack, where the timer previously stayed centred.
  • Developers: The iltk_breakpoints, iltk_fonts and iltk_block_classes filters replace twentig_breakpoints, twentig_fonts and twentig_block_classes. The old names still fire after the new ones and will be removed in a future release.

1.5.0

  • New: Grinner Text Rotator block — a line of text that cycles through a list, one item at a time. Pick a fade, blur, zoom or clip reveal, or the Pixel Reveal and Decrypt effects, and choose how long each item stays on screen.
  • New: Grinner Image Rotator block — a stepped image carousel showing up to six images at a time, advancing automatically, with arrows, or both. Seven transitions, from Slide and Fade to Centre Stage, Carousel Flow and a Card Drop deck. Its controls can stay visible, appear on hover or stay hidden, and hovering pauses the rotation unless you switch that off.
  • New: Script text effects for headings and paragraphs — Pixel Reveal, Line Reveal, Decrypt and Typewriter. They keep your inline text colours, hold the text’s exact layout so nothing around it moves, and stay still for visitors who prefer reduced motion. Decrypt’s pace and settle order are adjustable, and Typewriter’s blinking caret can be turned off.
  • New: Assemble entrance animation — words start scattered and blurred, then drift into place one after another.
  • New: Shuffle style for the number counter — each digit spins through random values before locking onto the final number.
  • New: “Above the fold” control on the Grinner Lottie block — turn it on for a hero animation so its poster image loads immediately as the page’s priority image, appearing at once while the animation initialises. Off by default; below-the-fold animations keep loading lazily.
  • Improved: Images from Grinner blocks now carry WordPress’s own responsive-image safety net, so they stay inside their space even before your page’s styles have finished loading.
  • Improved: New placeholder logos and images in the Logo Marquee, Image Slider and Image Rotator, so a freshly inserted block looks finished before you add your own.
  • Improved: Buttons with hover effects or decorations, clickable Group and Columns blocks, and the Before / After grip now respond visibly when pressed.
  • Improved: Every Grinner settings panel now uses one consistent spacing, so controls are easier to scan.
  • Improved: The caching FAQ now explains that on LiteSpeed-class optimisers with image lazy-loading, adding “ilm-eager” to the lazy-load exclusions lets the images Grinner Blocks marks to load immediately — hero posters and above-the-fold marquees — load right away instead of being deferred.
  • Fixed: The Video Embed poster no longer appears oversized for a moment before settling on sites that load stylesheets in the background.
  • Fixed: On sites that delay JavaScript until the visitor interacts, the first click on a video button now opens the lightbox instead of leaving for YouTube.

Earlier versions (1.4.2 and before) are listed in changelog.txt, included in the plugin.

short_description: Landing-page blocks for the block editor — sliders, countdowns, marquees, motion and more — with each block's code loaded only where it's used.
description:
See every block and effect in action at grinner.io.

Why Grinner Blocks

  • Performance-first: many blocks ship no JavaScript at all, and each block’s CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that use it.
  • Everything is included — no paid tier, no locked features.
  • Native blocks in the editor you already use. Deactivate the plugin and your posts keep their content; the controls added to core blocks simply switch off.
  • Landing-page features: content sliders, hover lists, card piles, progress bars, animated marquees, before/after sliders, counters, scroll reveals, avatar stacks and more.
  • You edit everything directly: place a block, drag it, change its text.

Everything you need to build landing pages

Grinner Blocks is a set of native blocks and controls for building and launching modern landing pages in WordPress. It lives inside the block editor you already use — no page builder, no jQuery. Every block renders on the server where it can, and each block’s own CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that use it. On block themes, the shared styles also load only where a page uses them, leaving about half a kilobyte site-wide; classic themes still load 82 KB of shared styles on every page.

Blocks

  • Before / After — two-image comparison slider, side by side or top and bottom, with a draggable divider driven by a real range input so it works with a keyboard and a screen reader. On touch screens the page still scrolls freely across it. Zero layout shift.
  • Avatar Stack — overlapping avatars for social proof, in a straight row or a gentle arc, with an optional “+N” chip, a trailing label and hover effects. It shrinks to fit narrow screens. No front-end JavaScript.
  • Logo Marquee — a continuous scrolling row of logos, pausing on hover, on keyboard focus and when scrolled off-screen.
  • Image Slider — the same continuous loop for photography, with fades, captions, hover effects and optional links. It can run along a curve (Arc, Smile, Drum or Wave), or stand still and let visitors swipe through it, looping endlessly.
  • Text Rotator — a line of text that cycles through a list, one item at a time, with fades, blurs, clip reveals or the Pixel Reveal and Decrypt effects — on a clock, or as the page scrolls. It can play an entrance animation first, its lines can carry formatting and accents, and it follows the alignment of the layout it sits in. Visitors who prefer reduced motion see the first item, still.
  • Image Rotator — a stepped carousel showing up to six images at a time, advancing on its own, with arrows, or both. Eight transitions (Carousel Flow can rest in an arc), plus layouts that arrange the images as a deck, a polaroid scatter, a mosaic, stepped columns, a spotlight with thumbnails or an orbit. Pause on hover, and no autoplay for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
  • Scrolling Text — a marquee for words, with separators, tilt and per-item styling.
  • Countdown — counts down to a date in any timezone, ticking live in the browser while a permanent screen-reader line states the real deadline.
  • Video Embed — a click-to-load YouTube facade using youtube-nocookie.com. Nothing from YouTube runs until the visitor clicks; a poster and play badge stand in until then.
  • Lottie — a self-hosted Lottie player supporting .json and .dotlottie, with loop / once / hover playback, a poster fallback and a mobile kill switch. The player library loads only when an animation starts, and you choose whether it starts once the page has loaded or on the visitor’s first touch or scroll.
  • Icon — one inline SVG icon from a bundled set of 1,512, rendered server-side in six weights.
  • Table — a responsive table built from real blocks, so each cell can hold anything, with an outer border and column widths.
  • Hover List — big link rows that show each row’s image on hover or keyboard focus. Five presets: a work index whose image follows the cursor, a split layout with one image area, a background swap, inline thumbnails, and expanding panels — an accordion that opens on hover, by click, tap or keyboard.
  • Content Slider — slides that hold any blocks (testimonials, features, case studies), moved by swipe, arrows, dots or autoplay. Four layouts: full width, several with a peek, a centred slide, or cards with a progress bar. It rewinds at the end instead of cloning slides, and its script loads only when arrows, dots or autoplay are on.
  • Card Pile — cards that stick and pile up as the page scrolls, for process steps or chapters. Four presets, CSS only, no JavaScript.
  • Progress Bar — labelled bars, thick bars, segments and steps, or rings, drawn in as the page scrolls or once in view. Values as a percentage, “42 of 60”, money or a rating, printed as real text.

Responsive layout controls

  • Set a maximum width per device — desktop, tablet and mobile — on headings, paragraphs, groups and columns.
  • Align a width-limited block left, centre or right with a box-alignment control.
  • Set how many columns a Grid block shows on desktop, tablet and mobile, with an optional gap for each.
  • Reorder the children of a Columns or Grid block on mobile without touching the desktop layout — per item, or with a one-switch reverse.
  • Choose when Columns stack: on phones only, on tablets as well, or two columns on tablets.

Block enhancements

Added as extra controls on the core blocks you already use:

  • Entrance animations and reveal-on-scroll for headings, paragraphs and groups, including the word-by-word Assemble effect, plus a number counter that counts up or shuffles its digits.
  • Accent text: select words and give them an accent from the toolbar — six ready-made styles built from your theme’s fonts and colours, or accents saved on your site — with highlights, underlines, circles, gradient or outline text and a draw-in animation. Each decoration has its own size and position controls, and changing an accent changes only the words you selected.
  • Grey to Colour: words go from muted to full colour as a heading or paragraph scrolls up the screen. No JavaScript, and the text is always readable.
  • Script text effects for headings and paragraphs — Pixel Reveal, Line Reveal, Decrypt and Typewriter — that hold the text’s exact layout while they run.
  • Button hover effects with their own fill and text colours, icons with their own colours, decorative corner marks, full-width fixes, vertical stacking, and click-to-play video buttons. On phones, a tapped button shows its hover colours while pressed and then returns to normal.
  • Navigation hover styles and markers, and item pills such as “New” or “Hot” beside a menu link; a sticky header with an optional glass effect.
  • A sticky call-to-action bar, whose buttons can stretch across the bar on phones, and clickable Group / Columns blocks: in a Query Loop each card can link to its own post, and a clickable card is one link and one Tab stop, while buttons to other pages still work on their own.
  • Layout reveals, text gradients and inline text icons.
  • Animated backgrounds for Group and Cover blocks: slow gradients, blobs and grain in your palette’s colours, paused off screen and still for reduced motion.
  • Link hover cards: internal links in paragraphs and lists can show a small preview card on hover or keyboard focus.
  • An aspect ratio and a rotation for the Group block, opacity for palette text colours, a paragraph pinned over its section, and Keep still for one child of a Parallax group.
  • Image effects on the core Image block: hover tilt, zoom, lift, greyscale and glare; parallax; entrances such as Rise, Wipe and Roll; and scroll effects such as zoom, tilt in and grey to colour. Images can also take a maximum width with limits, a resting angle, and stickers pinned over a section, still or animated.
  • A Loading setting on the Image, Cover and Post Featured Image blocks — Auto, Lazy, Eager or Priority — so you decide which image loads first. In a Query Loop, Priority applies to the first card only.

Site settings

  • Header and footer code injection, gated on the unfiltered_html capability.
  • Smooth anchor scrolling with a scroll offset for sticky headers.
  • Simple exact-match redirects.
  • A site-wide switch for animated previews inside the editor.
  • Preload the heading font (Performance): one preload for the font your main heading uses. Off by default.
  • An optional Excerpt field for pages, so Query Loop cards can show a summary you write.
  • A Data setting to keep or wipe your plugin data when you uninstall — off by default, so your data is kept.

Performance and accessibility

Every block’s CSS and JavaScript loads only on pages that actually use it, and the stylesheets and scripts visitors download carry no developer comments. The blocks use only font weights your site already loads, so they never add a font file. Many blocks ship no JavaScript at all, and one shared IntersectionObserver drives every scroll effect. Exactly one image per page is ever marked as the priority image, so nothing competes for the browser’s attention. Content is never hidden waiting for a script, even when a caching plugin delays JavaScript, and nothing Grinner Blocks animates can make a page scroll sideways on a phone. Animated content is hidden from screen readers and paired with a static equivalent, anything that moves on its own can be paused from the keyboard, and every animation stops for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

External services

Grinner Blocks connects to one external service, YouTube (operated by Google), and only on pages where you have added a YouTube video: a Grinner Video Embed block, or a click-to-play video on a button, an image or a Lottie animation. No other external service is contacted, and nothing is sent anywhere by the plugin’s own server code.

  • Video thumbnails. When a Grinner Video Embed block has no custom poster image, its poster is YouTube’s thumbnail for that video, loaded from i.ytimg.com when a visitor views the page, and in the editor while you edit the block. The request comes from the visitor’s browser, so YouTube receives the video ID, the visitor’s IP address and standard browser information. Choose a poster from your Media Library and no thumbnail request is made.
  • Video playback. The player loads from youtube-nocookie.com only after a visitor clicks play; before that click nothing from YouTube runs. On that click YouTube receives the video ID, the visitor’s IP address and standard browser information, and the player is then governed by YouTube’s own terms. If JavaScript is unavailable, the play button is a plain link to the video on youtube.com.

YouTube Terms of Service: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Source

All first-party Grinner Blocks code ships in this plugin as it was written: plain, human-readable PHP, JavaScript and CSS, with no compilation. This covers everything under blocks/, enhancements/, admin/, inc/blocks-layer2.php, inc/settings.php, inc/redirects.php, grinner-blocks.php and uninstall.php.

Since 1.7.0, visitors are served comment-free copies of the front-end stylesheets and scripts. Each copy (*.min.css, *.min.js) sits next to its readable source file in the same folder, and is made from it by removing only comments and extra whitespace: names, strings and code are unchanged. The copies are made by the plugin’s own build scripts, bin/build-css.js and bin/build-js.js (Node.js; the script build reads the code with the acorn parser to find what is a comment), which are development tools and are not included in the plugin. The readable file beside each copy is the source.

Three sets of files are pre-built third-party code. Their readable source lives upstream:

  • lottie-web 5.12.2 — blocks/lottie/assets/lottie.min.js is the official lottie_light.min.js build from release 5.12.2, unmodified (the “light” build omits the expression evaluator). Source: https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-web — released under the MIT license.
  • fflate 0.8.2 — blocks/lottie/assets/fflate.min.js is the official umd/index.js build from release 0.8.2, unmodified. Used to unpack .lottie archives in the browser. Source: https://github.com/101arrowz/fflate — released under the MIT license.
  • Twentig 2.0.1 — everything under dist/ is the built asset output of the Twentig plugin, version 2.0.1, which Grinner Blocks forks. Source: https://wordpress.org/plugins/twentig/ — released under GPL-3.0-or-later. Three files carry first-party modifications: in dist/index.css the editor icon embedded in it was changed from Twentig’s mark to the plugin’s own mark; in dist/style-index.css and dist/blocks/common.css the block entrance animation’s hidden starting state applies only once the plugin’s script has marked the page, so content is never left hidden when scripts are delayed or off. Upstream files the plugin does not use (starter-site templates and their preview images) are left out; every other file under dist/ is unchanged from the upstream 2.0.1 release.

The icon artwork data under enhancements/_shared/phosphor/ is generated from Phosphor Icons 2.1.1 (https://github.com/phosphor-icons/core, MIT) and ships as plain, readable JSON — see manifest.json there for the exact source version and generation date.

Credits

Grinner Blocks includes code from Twentig by Twentig.com, used under the GPL.

Bundled third-party libraries and their licenses are listed under Source, above.

upgrade_notice.1.8.0: Adds the Hover List, Content Slider, Card Pile and Progress Bar blocks, Image Rotator layouts, a curved Image Slider, a scroll-driven Text Rotator, animated backgrounds and link hover cards. Reduced motion now stops every moving block.
upgrade_notice.1.7.0: Adds Accent text, Grey to Colour, image effects, vertical Before / After, navigation pills and Loading on Cover and Featured Image. Some fixes change pages slightly: hover buttons use your button colour, padded Image Sliders fit their column, SVGs take their Max width as size.
upgrade_notice.1.6.1: Adds stickers on the Image block and Video Embed play button settings, supports WordPress 6.5 and later, and fixes Word by Word with formatted text and a Lottie that could stay on its poster.
upgrade_notice.1.6.0: The plugin is renamed Grinner Blocks and now requires PHP 8.0. Also adds the Image Rotator's Snap transition and fixes text effects painting outside their heading.
upgrade_notice.1.5.1: Fixes a fatal error when Grinner Blocks and Twentig are both active, blank sections with Drop or Swing stagger, parallax that froze in rounded groups, and Gradient sweep and Image zoom hovers that never showed. Adds a live Countdown preview and faster above-the-fold images. No breaking changes.
upgrade_notice.1.5.0: Adds the Text Rotator and Image Rotator blocks and four script text effects. Also fixes a Video Embed poster that could briefly appear oversized, and a first video click that could leave for YouTube on sites that delay JavaScript.
upgrade_notice.1.4.2: Fixes logo and image marquees that could animate or load incorrectly on sites with LiteSpeed or a similar optimisation plugin.
upgrade_notice.1.4.1: Editor polish: purple-branded block icons and consistent block titles, plus a rewritten listing. No functional changes.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0: Fixes a redirect save clearing your whole page cache, and stops delete-and-reinstall from wiping your saved redirects and injected code — that content now survives uninstall. Also adds responsive width and mobile-order controls. No breaking changes.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0: Adds the Before / After and Avatar Stack blocks, avatar hover effects, and an optional ripple on video play badges. New editor preview controls: a site-wide switch, a per-block toggle, and text animations that play once when you change a setting. No breaking changes.

instalaunch/lottie.name: instalaunch/lottie
instalaunch/lottie.title: Grinner Lottie
instalaunch/lottie.description: A self-hosted Lottie animation, lazy-initialised on scroll. Optional loop/once/hover playback and a click-to-play YouTube popup.

instalaunch/image-rotator.name: instalaunch/image-rotator
instalaunch/image-rotator.title: Grinner Image Rotator
instalaunch/image-rotator.description: A stepped image carousel: up to six images visible, manual and/or automatic advance, with a transition vocabulary from flat fades to a shuffled card deck.

instalaunch/before-after.name: instalaunch/before-after
instalaunch/before-after.title: Grinner Before / After
instalaunch/before-after.description: Two images compared with a draggable divider. Drag anywhere, click to jump, or use the arrow keys.

instalaunch/scrolling-text.name: instalaunch/scrolling-text
instalaunch/scrolling-text.title: Grinner Scrolling Text
instalaunch/scrolling-text.description: A continuous auto-scrolling strip of text items. CSS-only animation, zero JavaScript on the front end.

instalaunch/icon.name: instalaunch/icon
instalaunch/icon.title: Grinner Icon
instalaunch/icon.description: A single Phosphor icon in any of six weights. Decorative by default; add a label to make it meaningful, a link to make it clickable, or a background to make it a chip.

instalaunch/content-slider.name: instalaunch/content-slider
instalaunch/content-slider.title: Grinner Content Slider
instalaunch/content-slider.description: Slides that hold any blocks, in a native swipeable strip: full width, several with a peek, a centred slide or cards with a progress bar. Arrows, dots and autoplay load a small script only when switched on.

instalaunch/video-embed.name: instalaunch/video-embed
instalaunch/video-embed.title: Grinner Video Embed
instalaunch/video-embed.description: Click-to-load YouTube embed. A static poster shows first; the player iframe is built only on click — zero third-party iframe at page load.

instalaunch/avatar-stack.name: instalaunch/avatar-stack
instalaunch/avatar-stack.title: Grinner Avatar Stack
instalaunch/avatar-stack.description: Overlapping avatars for social proof, with an optional “+N more” chip and trailing label.

instalaunch/hover-list.name: instalaunch/hover-list
instalaunch/hover-list.title: Grinner Hover List
instalaunch/hover-list.description: A list of links that shows each row's image on hover or keyboard focus: a work index, a split image area, a background swap, inline thumbnails or expanding panels.

instalaunch/text-rotator.name: instalaunch/text-rotator
instalaunch/text-rotator.title: Grinner Text Rotator
instalaunch/text-rotator.description: A line of text that cycles through a list, one at a time, forever.

instalaunch/countdown.name: instalaunch/countdown
instalaunch/countdown.title: Grinner Countdown
instalaunch/countdown.description: A deadline countdown timer. Shows the real remaining time at first paint, then ticks live in the browser.

instalaunch/card-pile.name: instalaunch/card-pile
instalaunch/card-pile.title: Grinner Card Pile
instalaunch/card-pile.description: Cards that stack up as you scroll, each new card sliding over the last: a straight stack, a receding deck, dealt cards or split chapters. CSS only.

instalaunch/table.name: instalaunch/table
instalaunch/table.title: Grinner Table
instalaunch/table.description: A table-style grid whose cells hold real blocks, so dynamic data (Block Bindings) can resolve inside cells — unlike the core Table block.

instalaunch/marquee.name: instalaunch/marquee
instalaunch/marquee.title: Grinner Logo Marquee
instalaunch/marquee.description: A continuous auto-scrolling logo strip. CSS-only animation, zero JavaScript on the front end.

instalaunch/image-marquee.name: instalaunch/image-marquee
instalaunch/image-marquee.title: Grinner Image Slider
instalaunch/image-marquee.description: A continuous auto-scrolling image strip. CSS-only animation; a tiny script loads on the front end only when the manual-scroll infinite loop is enabled.

instalaunch/progress-bar.name: instalaunch/progress-bar
instalaunch/progress-bar.title: Grinner Progress Bar
instalaunch/progress-bar.description: A group of progress bars: thin labelled bars, thick bars with the value inside, segmented bars and steps, or rings. Values as a percentage, “42 of 60”, money or a rating.

instalaunch/content-slide.name: instalaunch/content-slide
instalaunch/content-slide.title: Grinner Slide
instalaunch/content-slide.description: One slide of a Grinner Content Slider. Holds any blocks.

instalaunch/card-pile-card.name: instalaunch/card-pile-card
instalaunch/card-pile-card.title: Grinner Pile Card
instalaunch/card-pile-card.description: One card in a Card Pile: an image, then an eyebrow, a heading, a line of text and a button.

instalaunch/table-cell.name: instalaunch/table-cell
instalaunch/table-cell.title: Table Cell
instalaunch/table-cell.description: One cell of the Grinner Table. Holds any blocks — headings, paragraphs, images.
